The heat flux is calculated using the total thermal resistance, and the interface temperature is found from the temperature drop across the inner convection and wood layer.

- Inside convective resistance: \(R_{\text{conv,in}} = 1/10 = 0.1 \, \text{m}^2\cdot\text{K/W}\)
- Wood conductive resistance: \(R_{\text{cond,1}} = 0.020/0.13 = 0.153846 \, \text{m}^2\cdot\text{K/W}\)
- Concrete conductive resistance: \(R_{\text{cond,2}} = 0.035/1.4 = 0.025 \, \text{m}^2\cdot\text{K/W}\)
- Outside convective resistance: \(R_{\text{conv,out}} = 1/23 \approx 0.0434783 \, \text{m}^2\cdot\text{K/W}\)
- Total resistance: \(R_{\text{total}} = 0.1 + 0.153846 + 0.025 + 0.0434783 = 0.322324 \, \text{m}^2\cdot\text{K/W}\)
- Temperature difference: \(\Delta T = 19 - (-18) = 37 \, \text{K}\)
- Heat flux: \(q = \Delta T / R_{\text{total}} = 37 / 0.322324 = 114.791 \, \text{W/m}^2\) → rounded to 4 significant figures: 114.8 W/m²
- Temperature drop from inside air to interface: \(\Delta T_{\text{in+wood}} = q \times (R_{\text{conv,in}} + R_{\text{cond,1}}) = 114.791 \times 0.253846 = 29.139 \, \text{K}\)
- Interface temperature: \(T_{\text{int}} = 19 - 29.139 = -10.139 \, ^\circ\text{C}\) → rounded to 4 significant figures: -10.14 °C

ANSWER: 114.8, -10.14
